rulings.grounds: tier-1 byte, re-derived independently: Prov.14.17 col-A ends אִוֶּ֑לֶת; Prov.14.18 col-A ends אִוֶּ֑לֶת -- the identical skeleton token is present at both verse-ends, so "no bridge exists" is false as a factual statement. sweep.py --skel אולת independently re-run: 22 verses book-wide, 6 within ch.14 alone (14:1, 14:8, 14:17, 14:18, 14:24, 14:29), confirming LF's digit and object exactly. Because the noun is this common (6/22 hits crowd into one chapter), it does not clear the §6 construction-run bar and the single_proverb boundary call for both P06-067 and P06-068 stays correct -- consistent with how this same writer part already treats other single shared nouns in this range (P06-067's מזמות precedent) as book vocabulary, not a driver. OL's support of P06-068 addressed a different claim (the inherit/crown verb pair) and never checked the rejected_alternative's "no bridge" sentence, so it is non-overlapping coverage, not a live conflict with LF's finding.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the rejected_alternative sentence to stop asserting "no bridge exists." Replace with an accurate disclosure: name the shared token (אִוֶּ֑לֶת) as a real but generic, book-wide wisdom-vocabulary link (22 verses book-wide / 6 in ch.14 alone: 14:1, 14:8, 14:17, 14:18, 14:24, 14:29) too diffuse to meet the §6 construction-run bar, so the single_proverb call for 14:17 and 14:18 each stands on that corrected ground rather than on a false absence-of-any-link claim. Test the cure must pass: the revised sentence may not claim zero lexical link where a shared token is byte-present at the seam (cross-seam cohesion disclosure rule) -- it must name the token, give both digits (book-wide and in-chapter), and state why the link is too weak to drive a cluster.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the span touches an undisclosed Ketiv/Qere at 14:21, and the 11:12 boundary_evidence_refs entry is never named by verse number in the row's own prose. OL: the same undisclosed K/Q at 14:21, plus the row's "to his neighbor" phrase claim blends two distinct shared objects (a common bare word vs. a rarer two-word construct) under one label.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes and pmarks: pmarks_Prov.json kq inventory carries Prov.14.21: 1; the oshb bytes confirm an inline ketiv/qere pair עניים עֲנָוִ֣ים sitting inside the row's own span (Prov.14.20-Prov.14.21) -- undisclosed in the row's prose or device_notes, a real defect under the book's unconditional span-relevant mark-disclosure rule. The row's rationale text ("occurs at only one further point, non-adjacent to this pair") indeed never states "11:12" as a digit despite 11:12 sitting in boundary_evidence_refs -- LF's orphan-citation point is confirmed by direct reading, independent of check_refs_mirror.py's WARN. OL's blended-object point is independently confirmed by re-running both sweeps: sweep.py --skel לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ (bare word underlying the row's "to his neighbor") returns exactly 3 verses book-wide (Prov.11.12, Prov.14.20, Prov.14.21) -- this bare, common word is what actually links the seam verses 14:20 (לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ, 2nd word) and 14:21 (לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ, 2nd word). Separately, the two-word verse-opening construct בָּז לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ that opens Prov.14.21 is skeleton-identical to Prov.11.12's own opener בָּז לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ: sweep.py --skel "בז לרעהו" returns exactly 2 verses book-wide, Prov.11.12 and Prov.14.21 ONLY -- and this sharper, rarer match is a link between 14:21 and the NON-adjacent 11:12, not between 14:20 and 14:21. The row's single undifferentiated "the phrase" label conflates these two distinct objects: the common bare word (which drives the 14:20-14:21 adjacency the row actually claims) and the rare two-word construct (which instead echoes a distant verse). This is the same class of error the TOOLKIT bans under SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE ("name the swept object FIRST ... blended sweeps forbidden"). The K/Q point is the SAME defect converged on by both primaries; the blended-object point is a DISTINCT additional defect OL alone caught.
rulings.remedy: One unified work order for the author wave, both objects named: (1) disclose the Prov.14.21 ketiv/qere note in device_notes or rationale (single-witness WLC, ketiv עניים / qere עֲנָוִ֣ים) since the row's span touches it; (2) name "11:12" as a digit in the prose sentence that currently reads "occurs at only one further point, non-adjacent to this pair" so the citation is textually anchored, not orphaned; (3) un-blend the catchword claim into two named objects instead of one "the phrase": (a) the bare word לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ/לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ ("to/of his neighbor"), 3 verses book-wide (11:12, 14:20, 14:21), which is the actual basis for the 14:20-14:21 adjacency the cluster call rests on; and (b) the two-word verse-opening construct בָּז לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ ("despises...his neighbor"), exactly 2 verses book-wide (11:12, 14:21 only), which is a sharper, rarer link between 14:21 and the non-adjacent 11:12 and must not be presented as evidence for the 14:20-14:21 seam itself. Test the cure must pass: check_marks.py span-symmetry (K/Q disclosed) and no single citation digit left covering two different named objects.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF (support): the fear-of-YHWH phrase (יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה) opens both 14:26 and 14:27 identically, book-wide unique adjacency among 15 sweep hits, meeting the construction-run bar. OL (challenge, high): the row's claim of an identical two-word construct filling an identical grammatical role is byte-false -- 14:26 opens bet-prefixed בְּיִרְאַ֣ת as an adverbial/prepositional modifier, 14:27 opens bare יִרְאַ֣ת as the clause subject -- and this false identity was load-bearing for ranking this pair's cohesion above the range's other catchword pairs.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently from consonantal_index.json and the pointed bytes: Prov.14.26 skeleton opens on the token ביראת (bet-prefixed); Prov.14.27 skeleton opens on יראת (bare) -- two different word-bound tokens, not one repeated phrase. Full bytes: Prov.14.26 = בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח עֹ֑ז ... ("in the fear of YHWH [is] strong confidence") -- the prefixed phrase is a prepositional/adverbial modifier and the clause subject is the following noun phrase (מִבְטַח עֹ֑ז); Prov.14.27 = יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים ... ("the fear of YHWH [is] a fountain of life") -- here the bare phrase itself is the clause subject. OL's grammatical-role description is confirmed exactly. Independently decomposing LF's own cited sweep (sweep.py --skel יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה = 15 book-wide) by word-boundedness: only 10 of the 15 carry the bare form (1:7, 2:5, 8:13, 9:10, 10:27, 14:27, 15:33, 19:23, 22:4, 31:30); the other 5 carry a proclitic prefix (1:29 ו-, 14:26 ב-, 15:16 ב-, 16:6 וב-, 23:17 ב-). NEITHER the bare-only subset NOR the prefixed-only subset contains a single adjacent pair anywhere in the book -- Prov.14.26/14.27 register as "adjacent" only because LF's substring sweep blended two different word-bound objects into one count of 15, exactly the "prefix-extension trap" the TOOLKIT hazard catalog names elsewhere (the טוב מ phrase-extension trap is the same class). LF's support is therefore refuted on the object level: it never checked word-boundedness before ranking this pair's cohesion above the cluster's other catchword pairs, which is exactly the load-bearing overclaim OL's challenge identifies.
rulings.remedy: Immediate disclosure-only cure (required regardless of any boundary outcome): rewrite rationale/device_notes/rejected_alternative to drop "the same two-word construct phrase ... functioning as the same grammatical subject." State instead, byte-grounded and object-named: 14:26 opens בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה (bet-prefixed, a prepositional/adverbial modifier of the clause's real subject, מִבְטַח עֹ֑ז "strong confidence"); 14:27 opens יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה (bare, itself the clause's grammatical subject of מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים "a fountain of life"). Any sweep citation must name the object first (bare vs. prefixed are different objects); a corrected sweep reports bare יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה = 10 verses (no adjacent pair anywhere) and prefixed forms = 5 verses (no adjacent pair anywhere) -- not a blended 15. The replacement warrant must pass the same prefix-variation test that killed the original: it may not re-assert unique adjacency using the blended 15-verse object, since that repeats the identical defect class one level removed (a forbidden blended sweep). Re-derivation here finds no word-bound adjacent match to substitute, so a bare 'cluster-with-corrected-warrant' is not available from the bytes as they stand. Flagged as a boss-adoption proposal, not decided here: with the false-identity claim removed, what remains is same-root recurrence (a construct of ירא + יהוה) opening two adjacent verses in two different constructions and grammatical roles -- closer to the §6-named 'shared THEME is over-clustering' pattern than to a true construction run (contrast the §6-named legitimate examples -- tov-min sayings, 26:4-5, the kings run -- which involve one identically repeated construction). The mesh/boss round should decide whether P06-075 reverts to two single_proverb rows (Prov.14.26, Prov.14.27, each keeping its own synthetic-parallelism device_notes) or whether a lighter-weight adjacent root-echo is affirmed as sufficient going forward -- an owner-level reading of the C2 construction-run bar, escalate-eligible.
